summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex bariatric history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal and prior gastrostomy tube removal) presented with two days of burning/sharp epigastric abdominal pain with nausea and poor oral intake after recently stopping her home acid-suppressing and mucosal-protective medications. Evaluation showed reassuring labs (including normal lipase), mild transaminase/alkaline phosphatase elevation that improved, and CT abdomen/pelvis without acute findings; abdominal radiograph showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern. Her course was notable for orthostatic hypotension with systolic blood pressures into the 80s that improved with IV normal saline and improved intake; AM cortisol was checked and was reassuring. Symptoms improved with scheduled acetaminophen, resumption of pantoprazole, ranitidine, and sucralfate, and an intensified bowel regimen (polyethylene glycol, bisacodyl, docusate, and PRN senna), along with nutrition counseling to use oral supplements. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable with return precautions and medication changes focused on gastritis management and hydration/nutrition.
